s01-title: Video ten: running on Kubernetes. Two pods, one gapless number sequence.
s02-deploy: Two kernel replicas run behind a Service, with a rolling update, max unavailable zero, and readiness and liveness probes. Two pods from the start, since tenancy and numbering must be cluster safe.
s03-parallel: Twelve orders are created at once, six on each pod. The order numbers run straight from seven to eighteen: no duplicates, no skipped numbers. Which pod gets which number is random, but the sequence stays continuous.
s04-desk: The same sequence, seen from Desk. The numbering pattern counts per tenant and per day.
s05-code: For developers: one upsert and one row lock. The second pod waits for the first pod's lock. If the transaction rolls back, so does the number: no gaps. No separate sequence, no Redis.
s06-rollout: A rolling restart with users online. A client reads orders every quarter second. During the restart there were forty-seven requests: forty-five returned two hundred, and two got no response as the old pod stopped.
s07-honest: To be accurate: nearly uninterrupted, not zero downtime. No preStop hook or drain time: requests to a stopping pod can fail. One Desk action may need a retry.
s99-recap: Recap: two replicas, gapless numbering with upsert and row lock, forty-five of forty-seven requests served in the restart. Next: Keycloak.
s10-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source, MIT license.
